title: R-rated director's cut of X-Files film restores Chris Carter's original horror vision
excerpt: Chris Carter chats with Ars about the film he originally wanted to make—and why it's more relevant than ever.

Chris Carter chats with Ars about the film he originally wanted to make—and why it’s more relevant than ever.

Credit: 20th Century Fox

There is a lot of excitement and some trepidation among The X-Files fans about Ryan Coogler’s reboot for Hulu, currently in production. While we’re waiting, Hulu just released Chris Carter’s revamped (and R-rated) director’s cut of the 2008 standalone spinoff film The X-Files: I Want to Believe, distinguishable from its predecessor with a slightly different title: The X-Files: I Want to Believe–Vrach Frankenshteyn.

(Minor spoilers below but no major reveals.)

I Want to Believe received mixed reviews at its release and didn’t exactly light up the box office, but it still grossed $68 million against its $30 million budget. By 2015, the project led to the return of The X-Files as a limited-run TV series, with the six-episode season 10 debuting in 2016. Mulder and Scully were reunited 14 years after the events of season 9 as the FBI reopened the X-Files under Assistant Director Walter Skinner (Mitch Pileggi). The response was strong enough to warrant a follow-up ten-episode season in 2018, focusing on Mulder and Scully’s search for their missing son, William.

So one could hardly call I Want to Believe a failure. I quite enjoyed the film, but I always had a niggling sense that something was missing. That suspicion was confirmed when Carter made an appearance on David Duchovny’s podcast last summer and revealed that the studio had insisted he cut numerous scenes to get the desired PG-13 rating. Carter also hinted that a director’s cut was in the offing. “I made it too scary,” Carter told Duchovny of his original vision. “Now I have a chance to go back and make the scary movie that I always intended.”

Originally slated for a June release on Disney+, I Want to Believe–Vrach Frankenshteyn eventually moved to Hulu with an August 14 release. It’s largely the same film as in 2008, just rejiggered to emphasize the stronger horror aspects that Carter originally envisioned. Per the official premise:

When a group of women is mysteriously abducted, it becomes a case right out of The X-Files. Years after walking away from the FBI, Fox Mulder and Dana Scully are pulled back from the shadows when a federal agent vanishes without a trace. In a case you’d never see on TV, their only lead is a disgraced, defrocked priest claiming to have horrific psychic visions of the crime. Forced to confront the ghosts of their past, the partners must navigate a chilling winter landscape and an even darker human monstrosity. The truth of these crimes is out there somewhere… and it will take Mulder and Scully to find it.

Ars Technica caught up with Carter to learn more.

Ars Technica: The original series always had some elements of horror. I’m curious about why you wanted to make a feature film that was more overtly horror with I Want to Believe.

Chris Carter: We certainly mined the horror genre over and over. The show always works at the intersection of science and science fiction. The original inspiration for this movie was that I read about a doctor who had done a head transplant from one monkey to another monkey’s body, and he’d done it successfully. Immediately I said, “That’s an X-File. I’ve got to tell that story.”

Of course, I wanted to tell it with human beings. So I flew to Cleveland, Ohio, where this doctor was, and he told me how he did it. It was successful, but ultimately the monkey died. But then I started thinking, “Well, maybe this is a way to live forever.” If you could transplant your head onto a younger person’s body, you could possibly keep doing that until something went wrong.

There’s this tech-bro fascination with living forever right now. So this story is as relevant now as it was back then. It’s a great time to tell this story. And I got to go back and revisit something that I was unable to make the way I wanted to make it, due to studio executives who really didn’t know the show. I had promised them I’d make a PG-13 movie because I thought, “That’s what I make on TV every week.” But it turns out that both the executives and the MPA, the people who do the ratings, are less permissive with a PG-13 movie than network television was with horror.

Ars Technica: There’s more to your director’s cut than just restoring a few deleted scenes. You’ve done a full re-edit.

Chris Carter: I worked with two different editors, people I respect and I’ve worked with before who weren’t involved with it all originally. I asked them to watch the movie and help me to refine the cut and make it the scary movie that I originally intended to make. It was heroic on their part. The movie was originally edited by an Academy Award winner, and so coming in and basically re-editing his vision took some courage.

That said, I think the editors alone, just in the way they re-approached the movie, really helped it. I gave them the reins early on, and then when they gave those cuts back to me, that’s when I started to work on it. They added material, they took out material, they restructured material. I wanted to make a good, scary movie. The [2008] movie was a relationship movie for Mulder and Scully that happened to have an X-Files case. The weighting was wrong, and I wanted to remaster that.

Ars Technica: Vrach Frankenshteyn is Russian for Doctor Frankenstein. You dabbled with that theme in the series occasionally as well. What keeps drawing you back to that particular well? 

Chris Carter: Creating life anew, breathing life into something that is inert, is fascinating to me. That story just fascinates me. The Mary Shelley story is much different than the original Frankenstein movie. They didn’t use lightning bolts to bring the creature to life. It was much more like an X-Files story. I’ve always drawn on my love of that story. Even if it’s not as pointedly like The Postmodern Prometheus, that science lives and breathes in several places in The X-Files.

Ars Technica: For many fans, Mulder and Scully will always be the beating heart of The X-Files. What makes them such an enduring couple, even if they are not always technically “together”? 

Chris Carter: Scully being a scientist and Mulder being a believer in the paranormal, and that they agree to disagree wonderfully—it’s part of the nature of their relationship. I think it’s their mutual respect for one another. That, for me, is the ideal man-woman relationship. It feels inevitable. It feels destined. I have that relationship with my wife. I believe in those connections, and I believe that everyone has a path. It’s just figuring out what path to take. Sometimes the path presents itself and you can’t see it. But with Mulder and Scully, they found their paths, and they’re traveling them together for better or worse.

Ars Technica: Back in 2008, you said that if I Want to Believe did well, there was a third X-Files film you were eager to make. Is that still ticking away in the back of your mind?

Chris Carter: It is ticking away in the back of my mind. If you watch the two reboots, there are four episodes [collectively] called “My Struggle.” They are the bookends for each of those series. They ended up in a place where people either loved me or hated me—when Scully revealed that she was pregnant. That is part of a bigger story, and I want to tell that story sometime. Right now, I think everyone’s focus is more on the Ryan Coogler reboot, and I don’t want to do anything to get in the way of that. I respect him, admire him, and want to see his vision. The story that I want to tell, if it is told—and I sure hope it will be—will be apart from that, but we certainly can’t ignore it.

Ars Technica: Did you envision when you created The X-Files that the series would become such a cultural touchstone for so many people? 

Chris Carter: No, I didn’t. I was sitting alone in my mid-30s. I’m working in Hollywood. I’ve been hired to create TV shows. I love movies like the Sherlock Holmes movie Murder by Decree. I love Kolchak: The Night Stalker. I have all these things that are inspiring me. I put them all together into a—call it a kiln. And I fired the kiln, and I opened it up and it’s The X-Files. I had never in my wildest dreams believed that I’d be sitting here talking to you today about The X-Files, that there’d be a Lego set coming out, that it would’ve changed people’s lives.

At the 30th reunion anniversary in Minneapolis, I had 12-year-old, 10-year-old kids come up and say they love the show. And I have to think to myself, “Your parents probably didn’t even know each other when the show first aired.”

I’ll tell you another story that is near and dear to me. My wife and I were running on the beach not long ago; we run for 10 minutes, and we walk for a minute. When we started walking in that minute, I look up and I see an image that I recognize immediately. I start walking toward this young woman in her early 20s who’s wearing a graduation gown and holding her mortarboard in her hand. On the top of the cap, it’s got an image of Mulder and Scully. And it says, “The future is out there.” I say, “I know that image.” She said, “Oh yeah, it’s Mulder and Scully from The X-Files.” And I said, “I know, I know. I wrote that show.”

It was a wonderful moment. She didn’t grow up with the show, she found the show. That’s the mind-blowing thing to me: it inspired her enough to put it on her graduation gown and cap. That kind of thing you can never imagine when you sit down to create something.

The X-Files: I Want to Believe–Vrach Frankenshteyn is now streaming on Disney+ and Hulu.

Jennifer is a senior writer at Ars Technica with a particular focus on where science meets culture, covering everything from physics and related interdisciplinary topics to her favorite films and TV series. Jennifer lives in Baltimore with her spouse, physicist Sean M. Carroll, and their two cats, Ariel and Caliban.

Forced to confront the ghosts of their past, the partners must navigate a chilling winter landscape and an even darker human monstrosity. The truth of these crimes is out there somewhere… and it will take Mulder and Scully to find it.

sentences.en: When a group of women is mysteriously abducted, it becomes a case right out of The X-Files.
sentences.zh: 一群妇女被神秘绑架，这就像《X 档案》中的案件一样。

sentences.en: Years after walking away from the FBI, Fox Mulder and Dana Scully are pulled back from the shadows when a federal agent vanishes without a trace.
sentences.zh: 离开联邦调查局多年后，一名联邦特工消失得无影无踪，福克斯·穆德和达纳·斯卡利从阴影中拉了回来。

sentences.en: In a case you’d never see on TV, their only lead is a disgraced, defrocked priest claiming to have horrific psychic visions of the crime.
sentences.zh: 在一个你永远不会在电视上看到的案件中，他们唯一的线索是一位名誉扫地、被解除圣职的牧师，他声称自己对这起犯罪行为有可怕的通灵幻象。

sentences.en: Forced to confront the ghosts of their past, the partners must navigate a chilling winter landscape and an even darker human monstrosity.
sentences.zh: 伙伴们被迫面对过去的幽灵，必须应对寒冷的冬季景观和更加黑暗的人类怪物。

sentences.en: The truth of these crimes is out there somewhere…
sentences.zh: 这些罪行的真相就在某个地方……

sentences.en: and it will take Mulder and Scully to find it.
sentences.zh: Mulder 和 Scully 需要找到它。

blocks.html_en: Ars Technica caught up with Carter to learn more.

sentences.en: Ars Technica caught up with Carter to learn more.
sentences.zh: Ars Technica 采访了卡特以了解更多信息。

blocks.html_en: Ars Technica: The original series always had some elements of horror. I’m curious about why you wanted to make a feature film that was more overtly horror with I Want to Believe.

sentences.en: Ars Technica: The original series always had some elements of horror.
sentences.zh: Ars Technica：原版系列总是带有一些恐怖元素。

sentences.en: I’m curious about why you wanted to make a feature film that was more overtly horror with I Want to Believe.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇你为什么想用《我想相信》制作一部更加明显的恐怖故事片。

blocks.html_en: Chris Carter: We certainly mined the horror genre over and over. The show always works at the intersection of science and science fiction. The original inspiration for this movie was that I read about a doctor who had done a head transplant from one monkey to another monkey’s body, and he’d done it successfully. Immediately I said, “That’s an X-File. I’ve got to tell that story.”

sentences.en: Chris Carter: We certainly mined the horror genre over and over.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·卡特：我们当然一遍又一遍地挖掘恐怖类型。

sentences.en: The show always works at the intersection of science and science fiction.
sentences.zh: 该剧始终处于科学与科幻小说的交叉点。

sentences.en: The original inspiration for this movie was that I read about a doctor who had done a head transplant from one monkey to another monkey’s body, and he’d done it successfully.
sentences.zh: 这部电影的最初灵感是我读到一位医生将一只猴子的头部移植到另一只猴子的身体上，而且他做得很成功。

sentences.en: Immediately I said, “That’s an X-File.
sentences.zh: 我立即说道：“那是一个 X 档案。

sentences.en: I’ve got to tell that story.”
sentences.zh: 我必须讲述这个故事。”

blocks.html_en: Of course, I wanted to tell it with human beings. So I flew to Cleveland, Ohio, where this doctor was, and he told me how he did it. It was successful, but ultimately the monkey died. But then I started thinking, “Well, maybe this is a way to live forever.” If you could transplant your head onto a younger person’s body, you could possibly keep doing that until something went wrong.

sentences.en: Of course, I wanted to tell it with human beings.
sentences.zh: 当然，我想用人类来讲述它。

sentences.en: So I flew to Cleveland, Ohio, where this doctor was, and he told me how he did it.
sentences.zh: 所以我飞往俄亥俄州克利夫兰，这位医生就在那里，他告诉我他是如何做到的。

sentences.en: It was successful, but ultimately the monkey died.
sentences.zh: 虽然成功了，但最终猴子还是死了。

sentences.en: But then I started thinking, “Well, maybe this is a way to live forever.”
sentences.zh: 但后来我开始想，“好吧，也许这是一种永生的方式。”

sentences.en: If you could transplant your head onto a younger person’s body, you could possibly keep doing that until something went wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果你可以将你的头移植到年轻人的身体上，你可能会一直这样做，直到出现问题为止。

blocks.html_en: There’s this tech-bro fascination with living forever right now. So this story is as relevant now as it was back then. It’s a great time to tell this story. And I got to go back and revisit something that I was unable to make the way I wanted to make it, due to studio executives who really didn’t know the show. I had promised them I’d make a PG-13 movie because I thought, “That’s what I make on TV every week.” But it turns out that both the executives and the MPA, the people who do the ratings, are less permissive with a PG-13 movie than network television was with horror.

sentences.en: There’s this tech-bro fascination with living forever right now.
sentences.zh: 现在科技界对永生有着浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: So this story is as relevant now as it was back then.
sentences.zh: 所以这个故事现在和当时一样具有现实意义。

sentences.en: It’s a great time to tell this story.
sentences.zh: 现在是讲述这个故事的好时机。

sentences.en: And I got to go back and revisit something that I was unable to make the way I wanted to make it, due to studio executives who really didn’t know the show.
sentences.zh: 我必须回去重新审视一些我无法按照我想要的方式制作的东西，因为工作室高管真的不了解这部剧。

sentences.en: I had promised them I’d make a PG-13 movie because I thought, “That’s what I make on TV every week.”
sentences.zh: 我答应他们我会制作一部 PG-13 电影，因为我想，“这就是我每周在电视上制作的电影。”

sentences.en: But it turns out that both the executives and the MPA, the people who do the ratings, are less permissive with a PG-13 movie than network television was with horror.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，高管们和 MPA（负责评级的人）对 PG-13 电影的宽容度不如网络电视对恐怖片的宽容度。

blocks.html_en: Ars Technica: There’s more to your director’s cut than just restoring a few deleted scenes. You’ve done a full re-edit.

sentences.en: Ars Technica: There’s more to your director’s cut than just restoring a few deleted scenes.
sentences.zh: Ars Technica：导演剪辑版不仅仅是恢复一些被删除的场景。

sentences.en: You’ve done a full re-edit.
sentences.zh: 您已经完成了完整的重新编辑。

blocks.html_en: Chris Carter: I worked with two different editors, people I respect and I’ve worked with before who weren’t involved with it all originally. I asked them to watch the movie and help me to refine the cut and make it the scary movie that I originally intended to make. It was heroic on their part. The movie was originally edited by an Academy Award winner, and so coming in and basically re-editing his vision took some courage.

sentences.en: Chris Carter: I worked with two different editors, people I respect and I’ve worked with before who weren’t involved with it all originally.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·卡特（Chris Carter）：我与两位不同的编辑一起工作，他们是我尊敬的人，也是我之前共事过的人，他们最初并没有参与这一切。

sentences.en: I asked them to watch the movie and help me to refine the cut and make it the scary movie that I originally intended to make.
sentences.zh: 我请他们看电影并帮助我完善剪辑，使其成为我原本打算拍的恐怖电影。

sentences.en: It was heroic on their part.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说这是英雄事迹。

sentences.en: The movie was originally edited by an Academy Award winner, and so coming in and basically re-editing his vision took some courage.
sentences.zh: 这部电影最初是由一位奥斯卡奖得主剪辑的，所以进来并基本上重新剪辑他的愿景需要一些勇气。

blocks.html_en: That said, I think the editors alone, just in the way they re-approached the movie, really helped it. I gave them the reins early on, and then when they gave those cuts back to me, that’s when I started to work on it. They added material, they took out material, they restructured material. I wanted to make a good, scary movie. The [2008] movie was a relationship movie for Mulder and Scully that happened to have an X-Files case. The weighting was wrong, and I wanted to remaster that.

sentences.en: That said, I think the editors alone, just in the way they re-approached the movie, really helped it.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我认为仅靠剪辑师重新处理这部电影的方式就确实起到了帮助作用。

sentences.en: I gave them the reins early on, and then when they gave those cuts back to me, that’s when I started to work on it.
sentences.zh: 我很早就把控制权交给了他们，然后当他们把这些削减权还给我时，我就开始着手处理它。

sentences.en: They added material, they took out material, they restructured material.
sentences.zh: 他们添加材料，删除材料，重组材料。

sentences.en: I wanted to make a good, scary movie.
sentences.zh: 我想拍一部好看的恐怖电影。

sentences.en: The [2008] movie was a relationship movie for Mulder and Scully that happened to have an X-Files case.
sentences.zh: 这部 [2008] 电影是一部穆德和斯卡利的爱情电影，恰好有一个 X 档案案件。

sentences.en: The weighting was wrong, and I wanted to remaster that.
sentences.zh: 权重是错误的，我想重新掌握它。

blocks.html_en: Ars Technica: Vrach Frankenshteyn is Russian for Doctor Frankenstein. You dabbled with that theme in the series occasionally as well. What keeps drawing you back to that particular well?

sentences.en: Ars Technica: Vrach Frankenshteyn is Russian for Doctor Frankenstein.
sentences.zh: Ars Technica：Vrach Frankenshteyn 是俄语，意为弗兰肯斯坦博士。

sentences.en: You dabbled with that theme in the series occasionally as well.
sentences.zh: 您偶尔也会在该系列中涉足该主题。

sentences.en: What keeps drawing you back to that particular well?
sentences.zh: 是什么让您不断回到那口井？

blocks.html_en: Chris Carter: Creating life anew, breathing life into something that is inert, is fascinating to me. That story just fascinates me. The Mary Shelley story is much different than the original Frankenstein movie. They didn’t use lightning bolts to bring the creature to life. It was much more like an X-Files story. I’ve always drawn on my love of that story. Even if it’s not as pointedly like The Postmodern Prometheus, that science lives and breathes in several places in The X-Files.

sentences.en: Chris Carter: Creating life anew, breathing life into something that is inert, is fascinating to me.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·卡特：重新创造生命，为惰性的东西注入生命，这对我来说很着迷。

sentences.en: That story just fascinates me.
sentences.zh: 这个故事让我着迷。

sentences.en: The Mary Shelley story is much different than the original Frankenstein movie.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·雪莱的故事与最初的弗兰肯斯坦电影有很大不同。

sentences.en: They didn’t use lightning bolts to bring the creature to life.
sentences.zh: 他们没有使用闪电来使该生物复活。

sentences.en: It was much more like an X-Files story.
sentences.zh: 这更像是一个X档案的故事。

sentences.en: I’ve always drawn on my love of that story.
sentences.zh: 我总是利用我对这个故事的热爱。

sentences.en: Even if it’s not as pointedly like The Postmodern Prometheus, that science lives and breathes in several places in The X-Files.
sentences.zh: 即使它不像《后现代普罗米修斯》那样尖锐，科学在《X档案》的几个地方仍然存在和呼吸。

blocks.html_en: Ars Technica: For many fans, Mulder and Scully will always be the beating heart of The X-Files. What makes them such an enduring couple, even if they are not always technically “together”?

sentences.en: Ars Technica: For many fans, Mulder and Scully will always be the beating heart of The X-Files.
sentences.zh: Ars Technica：对于许多粉丝来说，Mulder 和 Scully 永远是 X 档案的核心。

sentences.en: What makes them such an enduring couple, even if they are not always technically “together”?
sentences.zh: 是什么让他们成为如此长久的情侣，即使他们在技术上并不总是“在一起”？

blocks.html_en: Chris Carter: Scully being a scientist and Mulder being a believer in the paranormal, and that they agree to disagree wonderfully—it’s part of the nature of their relationship. I think it’s their mutual respect for one another. That, for me, is the ideal man-woman relationship. It feels inevitable. It feels destined. I have that relationship with my wife. I believe in those connections, and I believe that everyone has a path. It’s just figuring out what path to take. Sometimes the path presents itself and you can’t see it. But with Mulder and Scully, they found their paths, and they’re traveling them together for better or worse.

sentences.en: Chris Carter: Scully being a scientist and Mulder being a believer in the paranormal, and that they agree to disagree wonderfully—it’s part of the nature of their relationship.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·卡特：史高利是一名科学家，穆德是超自然现象的信徒，他们同意不同意见，这是他们关系本质的一部分。

sentences.en: I think it’s their mutual respect for one another.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是他们对彼此的相互尊重。

sentences.en: That, for me, is the ideal man-woman relationship.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这就是理想的男女关系。

sentences.en: It feels inevitable.
sentences.zh: 感觉这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: It feels destined.
sentences.zh: 感觉是命中注定。

sentences.en: I have that relationship with my wife.
sentences.zh: 我和我妻子有这种关系。

sentences.en: I believe in those connections, and I believe that everyone has a path.
sentences.zh: 我相信这些联系，我相信每个人都有一条路。

sentences.en: It’s just figuring out what path to take.
sentences.zh: 只是弄清楚要走哪条路。

sentences.en: Sometimes the path presents itself and you can’t see it.
sentences.zh: 有时，道路会自己出现，但你却看不到它。

sentences.en: But with Mulder and Scully, they found their paths, and they’re traveling them together for better or worse.
sentences.zh: 但与穆德和斯卡利一起，他们找到了自己的道路，并且无论好坏，他们都会一起走下去。

blocks.html_en: Ars Technica: Back in 2008, you said that if I Want to Believe did well, there was a third X-Files film you were eager to make. Is that still ticking away in the back of your mind?

sentences.en: Ars Technica: Back in 2008, you said that if I Want to Believe did well, there was a third X-Files film you were eager to make.
sentences.zh: Ars Technica：早在 2008 年，您就说过，如果《我想相信》表现出色，您就渴望制作第三部《X 档案》电影。

sentences.en: Is that still ticking away in the back of your mind?
sentences.zh: 这件事还在你的脑海里盘旋吗？

blocks.html_en: Chris Carter: It is ticking away in the back of my mind. If you watch the two reboots, there are four episodes [collectively] called “My Struggle.” They are the bookends for each of those series. They ended up in a place where people either loved me or hated me—when Scully revealed that she was pregnant. That is part of a bigger story, and I want to tell that story sometime. Right now, I think everyone’s focus is more on the Ryan Coogler reboot, and I don’t want to do anything to get in the way of that. I respect him, admire him, and want to see his vision. The story that I want to tell, if it is told—and I sure hope it will be—will be apart from that, but we certainly can’t ignore it.

sentences.en: Chris Carter: It is ticking away in the back of my mind.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·卡特：它在我的脑海里滴答作响。

sentences.en: If you watch the two reboots, there are four episodes [collectively] called “My Struggle.”
sentences.zh: 如果你看两部重启版，就会发现有四集（统称为“我的奋斗”）。

sentences.en: They are the bookends for each of those series.
sentences.zh: 它们是每个系列的书挡。

sentences.en: They ended up in a place where people either loved me or hated me—when Scully revealed that she was pregnant.
sentences.zh: 当斯卡利透露她怀孕了时，他们最终陷入了人们要么爱我要么恨我的境地。

sentences.en: That is part of a bigger story, and I want to tell that story sometime.
sentences.zh: 这是一个更大故事的一部分，我想找个时间讲述这个故事。

sentences.en: Right now, I think everyone’s focus is more on the Ryan Coogler reboot, and I don’t want to do anything to get in the way of that.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为每个人的注意力更多地集中在瑞恩·库格勒的重启上，我不想做任何事情来妨碍这一点。

sentences.en: I respect him, admire him, and want to see his vision.
sentences.zh: 我尊重他，钦佩他，希望看到他的远见。

sentences.en: The story that I want to tell, if it is told—and I sure hope it will be—will be apart from that, but we certainly can’t ignore it.
sentences.zh: 我想讲述的故事，如果被讲述——我当然希望如此——将与此不同，但我们当然不能忽视它。

blocks.html_en: Ars Technica: Did you envision when you created The X-Files that the series would become such a cultural touchstone for so many people?

sentences.en: Ars Technica: Did you envision when you created The X-Files that the series would become such a cultural touchstone for so many people?
sentences.zh: Ars Technica：当您创作《X档案》时，您有没有想过该系列将成为这么多人的文化试金石？

blocks.html_en: Chris Carter: No, I didn’t. I was sitting alone in my mid-30s. I’m working in Hollywood. I’ve been hired to create TV shows. I love movies like the Sherlock Holmes movie Murder by Decree. I love Kolchak: The Night Stalker. I have all these things that are inspiring me. I put them all together into a—call it a kiln. And I fired the kiln, and I opened it up and it’s The X-Files. I had never in my wildest dreams believed that I’d be sitting here talking to you today about The X-Files, that there’d be a Lego set coming out, that it would’ve changed people’s lives.

sentences.en: Chris Carter: No, I didn’t.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·卡特：不，我没有。

sentences.en: I was sitting alone in my mid-30s.
sentences.zh: 我三十多岁，独自一人坐着。

sentences.en: I’m working in Hollywood.
sentences.zh: 我在好莱坞工作。

sentences.en: I’ve been hired to create TV shows.
sentences.zh: 我受聘制作电视节目。

sentences.en: I love movies like the Sherlock Holmes movie Murder by Decree.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢像夏洛克·福尔摩斯电影《法令谋杀》这样的电影。

sentences.en: I love Kolchak: The Night Stalker.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢高尔察克：夜行者。

sentences.en: I have all these things that are inspiring me.
sentences.zh: 我拥有所有这些激励我的事情。

sentences.en: I put them all together into a—call it a kiln.
sentences.zh: 我把它们全部放在一个——称之为窑炉中。

sentences.en: And I fired the kiln, and I opened it up and it’s The X-Files.
sentences.zh: 我点燃了窑炉，打开它，这是《X档案》。

sentences.en: I had never in my wildest dreams believed that I’d be sitting here talking to you today about The X-Files, that there’d be a Lego set coming out, that it would’ve changed people’s lives.
sentences.zh: 在我最疯狂的梦想中，我从未相信我今天会坐在这里与大家谈论《X档案》，相信会有乐高积木套装问世，相信它会改变人们的生活。

blocks.html_en: At the 30th reunion anniversary in Minneapolis, I had 12-year-old, 10-year-old kids come up and say they love the show. And I have to think to myself, “Your parents probably didn’t even know each other when the show first aired.”

sentences.en: At the 30th reunion anniversary in Minneapolis, I had 12-year-old, 10-year-old kids come up and say they love the show.
sentences.zh: 在明尼阿波利斯举行的 30 周年聚会纪念日上，我让 12 岁、10 岁的孩子上来说他们喜欢这个节目。

sentences.en: And I have to think to myself, “Your parents probably didn’t even know each other when the show first aired.”
sentences.zh: 我不得不对自己说，“当节目第一次播出时，你的父母可能根本不认识。”

blocks.html_en: I’ll tell you another story that is near and dear to me. My wife and I were running on the beach not long ago; we run for 10 minutes, and we walk for a minute. When we started walking in that minute, I look up and I see an image that I recognize immediately. I start walking toward this young woman in her early 20s who’s wearing a graduation gown and holding her mortarboard in her hand. On the top of the cap, it’s got an image of Mulder and Scully. And it says, “The future is out there.” I say, “I know that image.” She said, “Oh yeah, it’s Mulder and Scully from The X-Files.” And I said, “I know, I know. I wrote that show.”

sentences.en: I’ll tell you another story that is near and dear to me.
sentences.zh: 我要告诉你另一个我很亲近的故事。

sentences.en: My wife and I were running on the beach not long ago; we run for 10 minutes, and we walk for a minute.
sentences.zh: 不久前，我和妻子在海滩上跑步；我们跑10分钟，步行1分钟。

sentences.en: When we started walking in that minute, I look up and I see an image that I recognize immediately.
sentences.zh: 当我们开始走路的那一刻，我抬起头，看到了一个我立即认出的图像。

sentences.en: I start walking toward this young woman in her early 20s who’s wearing a graduation gown and holding her mortarboard in her hand.
sentences.zh: 我开始走向这位 20 岁出头的年轻女子，她穿着毕业礼服，手里拿着学位帽。

sentences.en: On the top of the cap, it’s got an image of Mulder and Scully.
sentences.zh: 帽子的顶部有 Mulder 和 Scully 的图像。

sentences.en: And it says, “The future is out there.”
sentences.zh: 它说：“未来就在那里。”

sentences.en: I say, “I know that image.”
sentences.zh: 我说：“我知道那个图像。”

sentences.en: She said, “Oh yeah, it’s Mulder and Scully from The X-Files.”
sentences.zh: 她说：“哦，是的，这是《X档案》中的穆德和斯卡利。”

sentences.en: And I said, “I know, I know.
sentences.zh: 我说：“我知道，我知道。

sentences.en: I wrote that show.”
sentences.zh: 那个节目是我写的。”

blocks.html_en: It was a wonderful moment. She didn’t grow up with the show, she found the show. That’s the mind-blowing thing to me: it inspired her enough to put it on her graduation gown and cap. That kind of thing you can never imagine when you sit down to create something.

sentences.en: It was a wonderful moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个美妙的时刻。

sentences.en: She didn’t grow up with the show, she found the show.

克里斯·卡特 (Chris Carter) 与 Ars 讨论了他最初想要制作的电影，以及为什么它比以往任何时候都更重要。

图片来源：20 世纪福克斯

《X 档案》的粉丝们对瑞安·库格勒 (Ryan Coogler) 重启的 Hulu（目前正在制作中）既兴奋又有些惶恐。 在我们等待的同时，Hulu 刚刚发布了克里斯·卡特 (Chris Carter) 对 2008 年独立衍生电影《X 档案：我想相信》的改编版（R 级）导演剪辑版，与前作的标题略有不同：《X 档案：我想相信 – 弗拉赫·弗兰肯斯坦》。

（以下有轻微剧透，但没有透露重大内容。）

《我想相信》上映时获得了褒贬不一的评价，票房也没有完全亮起来，但相对于 3000 万美元的预算，它仍然获得了 6800 万美元的票房收入。 到 2015 年，该项目导致《X 档案》作为限量版电视剧回归，共 6 集的第 10 季于 2016 年首播。 第九季事件发生 14 年后，联邦调查局在助理局长沃尔特·斯金纳（米奇·皮莱吉饰）的带领下重新打开了 X 档案，穆德和斯高利重聚。 反响强烈，值得在 2018 年制作后续的十集剧集，重点讲述穆德和斯卡利寻找失踪儿子威廉的故事。

因此，很难说《我想相信》是一部失败之作。 我非常喜欢这部电影，但我总有一种微妙的感觉，好像缺少了一些东西。 去年夏天卡特出现在大卫·杜楚尼的播客上并透露工作室坚持要求他剪掉大量场景以获得理想的 PG-13 评级时，这一怀疑得到了证实。 卡特还暗示导演剪辑版即将推出。 “我把它做得太可怕了，”卡特告诉杜楚尼他最初的愿景。 “现在我有机会回去制作我一直想要的恐怖电影。”

《I Want to Believe – Vrach Frankenshteyn》原定于 6 月在 Disney+ 上发布，但最终转移到 Hulu，并于 8 月 14 日发布。 这部电影与 2008 年的电影基本相同，只是进行了重新调整，以强调卡特最初设想的更强烈的恐怖元素。 根据官方前提：

一群妇女被神秘绑架，这就像《X 档案》中的案件一样。 离开联邦调查局多年后，一名联邦特工消失得无影无踪，福克斯·穆德和达纳·斯卡利从阴影中拉了回来。 在一个你永远不会在电视上看到的案件中，他们唯一的线索是一位名誉扫地、被解除圣职的牧师，他声称自己对这起犯罪行为有可怕的通灵幻象。 伙伴们被迫面对过去的幽灵，必须应对寒冷的冬季景观和更加黑暗的人类怪物。 这些罪行的真相就在某个地方…… Mulder 和 Scully 需要找到它。

Ars Technica 采访了卡特以了解更多信息。

Ars Technica：原版系列总是带有一些恐怖元素。 我很好奇你为什么想用《我想相信》制作一部更加明显的恐怖故事片。

克里斯·卡特：我们当然一遍又一遍地挖掘恐怖类型。 该剧始终处于科学与科幻小说的交叉点。 这部电影的最初灵感是我读到一位医生将一只猴子的头部移植到另一只猴子的身体上，而且他做得很成功。 我立即说道：“那是一个 X 档案。 我必须讲述这个故事。”

当然，我想用人类来讲述它。 所以我飞往俄亥俄州克利夫兰，这位医生就在那里，他告诉我他是如何做到的。 虽然成功了，但最终猴子还是死了。 但后来我开始想，“好吧，也许这是一种永生的方式。” 如果你可以将你的头移植到年轻人的身体上，你可能会一直这样做，直到出现问题为止。

现在科技界对永生有着浓厚的兴趣。 所以这个故事现在和当时一样具有现实意义。 现在是讲述这个故事的好时机。 我必须回去重新审视一些我无法按照我想要的方式制作的东西，因为工作室高管真的不了解这部剧。 我答应他们我会制作一部 PG-13 电影，因为我想，“这就是我每周在电视上制作的电影。” 但事实证明，高管们和 MPA（负责评级的人）对 PG-13 电影的宽容度不如网络电视对恐怖片的宽容度。

Ars Technica：导演剪辑版不仅仅是恢复一些被删除的场景。 您已经完成了完整的重新编辑。

克里斯·卡特（Chris Carter）：我与两位不同的编辑一起工作，他们是我尊敬的人，也是我之前共事过的人，他们最初并没有参与这一切。 我请他们看电影并帮助我完善剪辑，使其成为我原本打算拍的恐怖电影。 对他们来说这是英雄事迹。 这部电影最初是由一位奥斯卡奖得主剪辑的，所以进来并基本上重新剪辑他的愿景需要一些勇气。

也就是说，我认为仅靠剪辑师重新处理这部电影的方式就确实起到了帮助作用。 我很早就把控制权交给了他们，然后当他们把这些削减权还给我时，我就开始着手处理它。 他们添加材料，删除材料，重组材料。 我想拍一部好看的恐怖电影。 这部 [2008] 电影是一部穆德和斯卡利的爱情电影，恰好有一个 X 档案案件。 权重是错误的，我想重新掌握它。

Ars Technica：Vrach Frankenshteyn 是俄语，意为弗兰肯斯坦博士。 您偶尔也会在该系列中涉足该主题。 是什么让您不断回到那口井？

克里斯·卡特：重新创造生命，为惰性的东西注入生命，这对我来说很着迷。 这个故事让我着迷。 玛丽·雪莱的故事与最初的弗兰肯斯坦电影有很大不同。 他们没有使用闪电来使该生物复活。 这更像是一个X档案的故事。 我总是利用我对这个故事的热爱。 即使它不像《后现代普罗米修斯》那样尖锐，科学在《X档案》的几个地方仍然存在和呼吸。

Ars Technica：对于许多粉丝来说，Mulder 和 Scully 永远是 X 档案的核心。 是什么让他们成为如此长久的情侣，即使他们在技术上并不总是“在一起”？

克里斯·卡特：史高利是一名科学家，穆德是超自然现象的信徒，他们同意不同意见，这是他们关系本质的一部分。 我认为这是他们对彼此的相互尊重。 对我来说，这就是理想的男女关系。 感觉这是不可避免的。 感觉是命中注定。 我和我妻子有这种关系。 我相信这些联系，我相信每个人都有一条路。 只是弄清楚要走哪条路。 有时，道路会自己出现，但你却看不到它。 但与穆德和斯卡利一起，他们找到了自己的道路，并且无论好坏，他们都会一起走下去。

Ars Technica：早在 2008 年，您就说过，如果《我想相信》表现出色，您就渴望制作第三部《X 档案》电影。 这件事还在你的脑海里盘旋吗？

克里斯·卡特：它在我的脑海里滴答作响。 如果你看两部重启版，就会发现有四集（统称为“我的奋斗”）。 它们是每个系列的书挡。 当斯卡利透露她怀孕了时，他们最终陷入了人们要么爱我要么恨我的境地。 这是一个更大故事的一部分，我想找个时间讲述这个故事。 现在，我认为每个人的注意力更多地集中在瑞恩·库格勒的重启上，我不想做任何事情来妨碍这一点。 我尊重他，钦佩他，希望看到他的远见。 我想讲述的故事，如果被讲述——我当然希望如此——将与此不同，但我们当然不能忽视它。

Ars Technica：当您创作《X档案》时，您有没有想过该系列将成为这么多人的文化试金石？

克里斯·卡特：不，我没有。 我三十多岁，独自一人坐着。 我在好莱坞工作。 我受聘制作电视节目。 我喜欢像夏洛克·福尔摩斯电影《法令谋杀》这样的电影。 我喜欢高尔察克：夜行者。 我拥有所有这些激励我的事情。 我把它们全部放在一个——称之为窑炉中。 我点燃了窑炉，打开它，这是《X档案》。 在我最疯狂的梦想中，我从未相信我今天会坐在这里与大家谈论《X档案》，相信会有乐高积木套装问世，相信它会改变人们的生活。

在明尼阿波利斯举行的 30 周年聚会纪念日上，我让 12 岁、10 岁的孩子上来说他们喜欢这个节目。 我不得不对自己说，“当节目第一次播出时，你的父母可能根本不认识。”

我要告诉你另一个我很亲近的故事。 不久前，我和妻子在海滩上跑步；我们跑10分钟，步行1分钟。 当我们开始走路的那一刻，我抬起头，看到了一个我立即认出的图像。 我开始走向这位 20 岁出头的年轻女子，她穿着毕业礼服，手里拿着学位帽。 帽子的顶部有 Mulder 和 Scully 的图像。 它说：“未来就在那里。” 我说：“我知道那个图像。” 她说：“哦，是的，这是《X档案》中的穆德和斯卡利。” 我说：“我知道，我知道。 那个节目是我写的。”

这是一个美妙的时刻。 她并不是随着这部剧长大的，而是她发现了这部剧。 这对我来说是令人兴奋的事情：它给了她足够的灵感，把它戴在了她的毕业礼服和帽子上。 当你坐下来创造一些东西时，你永远无法想象这种事情。

《X 档案：我想相信 – 弗拉赫·弗兰肯斯坦》现已在 Disney+ 和 Hulu 上播出。

Jennifer 是 Ars Technica 的资深作家，特别关注科学与文化的交汇，内容涵盖从物理学和相关跨学科主题到她最喜欢的电影和电视剧等各个领域。 詹妮弗 (Jennifer) 与她的配偶物理学家肖恩·M·肖恩 (Sean M. 卡罗尔和他们的两只猫，爱丽儿和卡利班。
